parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian антихристъ (antixrist), from Old East Slavic антихристъ (antixristŭ), from Old Church Slavonic антихрьстъ (antixrĭstŭ), from Koine Greek ἀντίχριστος (antíkhristos).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian беззаконие (bezzakonje), from Old East Slavic беззакониѥ (bezzakonije), probably from Old Church Slavonic безакониѥ (bezakonije), itself likely a calque of Koine Greek ἀνομία (anomía). By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + зако́н (zakón) + -я (-ja). Compare Russian беззако́

parole.significato: Caesar (title of a Roman or Byzantine emperor)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic кесар (kesar), from Koine Greek Καῖσαρ (Kaîsar), itself a borrowing from Latin Caesar. Doublet of цар (car), це́зар (cézar), and це́сар (césar).

Learned borrowing from Old Church Slavonic серафимъ (serafimŭ), from Koine Greek σεραφείμ (serapheím), from Biblical Hebrew שְׂרָפִים (śərāp̄îm), the plural form of שָׂרָף (śārāp̄), often translated as "fiery ones", although meaning is uncertain; perhaps related to the root שרף (“to burn”).
